## claude.ai Datadog
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). Consult Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Use when the user says "integrate agent", "add agent support", or wants to run the full agent integration pipeline end-to-end.

For individual phases, use /e2e:triage-ci, /e2e:debug, or /e2e:implement. Use when the user says "triage e2e", "fix e2e failures", or wants the full triage-to-fix pipeline.
- test-repo: Use this skill to test strategy changes against a fresh test repository. Invoke when the user asks to "test against a test repo", "validate the changes", or wants to verify session hooks, commits, and rewind functionality work correctly.

- dev-cycle: Orchestrates the development cycle - developer implements, reviewer critiques, repeat until done

- commit-commands:commit-push-pr: Commit, push, and open a PR
- commit-commands:commit: Create a git commit
- codex:rescue: Delegate investigation, an explicit fix request, or follow-up rescue work to the Codex rescue subagent

- e2e:debug: Deep-dive artifact analysis for diagnosing E2E test failures

- superpowers:requesting-code-review: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements
- superpowers:subagent-driven-development: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session
- superpowers:systematic-debugging: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
- superpowers:test-driven-development: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code
- superpowers:using-git-worktrees: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - ensures an isolated workspace exists via native tools or git worktree fallback
- superpowers:using-superpowers: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
- superpowers:verification-before-completion: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
- superpowers:writing-plans: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code

- codex:codex-result-handling: Internal guidance for presenting Codex helper output back to the user
- codex:gpt-5-4-prompting: Internal guidance for composing Codex and GPT-5.4 prompts for coding, review, diagnosis, and research tasks inside the Codex Claude Code plugin
- entire:address-findings: Address the review findings posted on an Entire trail: fetch the trail's open findings, fix the code, and resolve them on the trail. Use when the user gives a trail URL or number and asks to address, fix, or resolve its findings or review comments. Not for local diff review — that is the `review` skill.
- entire:explain: Explains the intent behind source code by finding original session transcripts. Use explain with a function, file, or line of code to understand why it exists.
- entire:recall: Use when the user describes a task and wants to know whether something similar has been done before, then turn the closest prior session into a task playbook. Triggers on phrases like "have we done this before", "recall how we did X", "find similar work", "any precedent for", "has anyone solved", "is there a template for", and "how did we do this last time"
- entire:replay: Use when the user wants to step through a feature's checkpoints chronologically, pausing at each step to ask questions. Triggers on phrases like "replay <feature>", "walk me through how X was built", "show me the journey of", "step me through how Y was implemented", and "replay the last week"
- entire:review: Review code changes on the current branch using checkpoint transcript context to understand developer intent before auditing the diff. Use when the user asks for a code review, wants to review branch changes, or asks to audit recent work before merging.
- entire:search: Use when the user wants to find prior work, checkpoints, or agent conversations by topic, repo, branch, author, or recent time window, or to search code content across repositories
- entire:session-crosslink: Use when an agent session ran outside the repo whose commits should record it — e.g. launched from a higher-level folder, a non-Entire repo, or one repo but editing another — to attach the session to each affected Entire-enabled repo's HEAD commit.
- entire:session-handoff: Use when the user wants to continue work from one agent in another agent, inspect recent sessions, or summarize a saved session or checkpoint for handoff
- entire:session-to-skill: Use when the user wants to turn one or more Entire-tracked sessions, checkpoints, or repeated agent workflows into a reusable agent skill.
- entire:teach: Use when a developer wants a topic-focused guided lesson built from canonical checkpoints, not a whole-repo overview. Triggers on phrases like "teach me <topic>", "teach me how this repo handles", "how does <topic> work in this repo", "give me a lesson on", "school me on", and "I need to learn about"
- entire:using-entire: Use for any codebase exploration or understanding task — reads historical intent from Entire checkpoints instead of guessing. Orchestrates other Entire skills to give the agent provenance-backed answers about code.
- entire:what-happened: Explain why code looks the way it does by tracing the latest change for a file range or pasted snippet through `git blame` and deduplicated `entire explain` lookups. Use when the user asks what happened, says "tell me why" about a code block, is confused about a section of code, asks "wtf is going on", "why is this like this", "why was this changed", or wants provenance for a specific file block.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

{"id":"ENCLI-333","title":"blobOnDisk probes trigger git lazy fetch in partial clones — one network fetch per missing blob per remote","description":"`FetchingTree.blobOnDisk` (`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/fetching_tree.go:193`) checks blob presence with a bare `git cat-file -e <hash>`:

```go
cmd := exec.CommandContext(t.ctx, "git", "cat-file", "-e", hash.String())
return cmd.Run() == nil
```

In a partial clone, `cat-file -e` on an absent object triggers git's internal lazy fetch: a single-want upload-pack request against each configured promisor remote before returning nonzero. The comment above the function says the check exists to "skip a wasted network round-trip" — it instead performs up to two per missing blob, each spawning `git-remote-entire` (~1s).

`CollectMissingBlobs` calls this for every blob entry in the checkpoint subtree, so one `entire explain` on a checkpoint whose blobs were never pushed produced ~1,800 upload-pack requests and a git-protocol SLO P1 (see parent issue).

## Fix

* Run the probe with `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` in the child env so `cat-file -e` answers from the local object store only.
* Batch all hashes through one `git cat-file --batch-check` process (same env) instead of one spawn per blob.

{"id":"ENCLI-335","title":"git-remote-entire: cap and back off retries for unservable wants","description":"`git-remote-entire` retries a failed want with no backoff and no ceiling, and the `entireio/cli` pre-push hook's `|| true` hides the failure entirely. When the server answers `503` + `Retry-After: 5` for a want it has never held (the <issue id="99c35963-dd1b-4bf4-a691-66c80401f30e" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1939/decide-whether-to-flip-the-missing-want-503-default">ENT-1939</issue> misclassification), the client can never succeed and never stops.

No server status-code change fixes a client that never gives up — even after <issue id="99c35963-dd1b-4bf4-a691-66c80401f30e" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1939/decide-whether-to-flip-the-missing-want-503-default">ENT-1939</issue> flips bogus wants to a terminal 400, transient-looking failures still deserve a bounded retry budget.

## Fix

* Honor a total retry budget (attempts or wall-clock) per want/fetch, with exponential backoff between attempts.
* Surface the terminal failure instead of swallowing it (`|| true` in the pre-push hook).

Carved out of <issue id="99c35963-dd1b-4bf4-a691-66c80401f30e" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1939/decide-whether-to-flip-the-missing-want-503-default">ENT-1939</issue>'s "follow-ups this does not cover".","priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENCLI-335/git-remote-entire-cap-and-back-off-retries-for-unservable-wants","gitBranchName":"evis/encli-335-git-remote-entire-cap-and-back-off-retries-for-unservable","createdAt":"2026-08-26T22:51:59.104Z","updatedAt":"2026-08-26T22:51:59.104Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"f7107ac2-0e19-4339-9252-983beda3ff0b","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-26T22:51:59.104Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Evis Drenova","createdById":"bd1c458e-3bb3-4d0c-8ad7-e36f19afc156","parentId":"ENT-1990","team":"entire-cli OSS","teamId":"ef5b8f96-81e4-4a76-bd29-11a1b431e339"}

1	package checkpoint
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"io"
7		"log/slog"
8		"os/exec"
9	
10		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
11	
12		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
13		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing/object"
14		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing/storer"
15	)
16	
17	// BlobFetchFunc fetches missing blob objects by hash from a remote.
18	type BlobFetchFunc func(ctx context.Context, hashes []plumbing.Hash) error
19	
20	// RefFetchFunc fetches a single checkpoint ref from the remote into the local
21	// ref of the same name. The git-refs store uses it to resolve a checkpoint ref
22	// that is not present locally (e.g. written on another machine). The checkpoint
23	// package cannot resolve the remote target itself, so the CLI layer injects it.
24	type RefFetchFunc func(ctx context.Context, ref plumbing.ReferenceName) error
25	
26	// MetadataBranchFetchFunc fetches the v1 metadata branch from the configured
27	// checkpoint remote into the local ref. It is the git-branch store's counterpart
28	// to RefFetchFunc: the git-refs store resolves one missing per-checkpoint ref,
29	// while the git-branch store's whole record lives on a single branch, so a
30	// missing local branch is resolved by fetching that branch.
31	//
32	// Without it, a clone whose checkpoints live on a dedicated checkpoint_remote
33	// cannot read any committed checkpoint until something else happens to populate
34	// the branch: the store falls back to origin's remote-tracking ref, which a
35	// checkpoint_remote setup does not have. The checkpoint package cannot resolve
36	// the remote target itself, so the CLI layer injects it.
37	//
38	// Only wire it on foreground, user-initiated read paths. It fires only when the
39	// branch is missing both locally and on origin — i.e. when the read would
40	// otherwise fail outright — but it is still a network call, and hook paths must
41	// stay network-free.
42	type MetadataBranchFetchFunc func(ctx context.Context) error
43	
44	// RemoteRefListFunc enumerates the per-checkpoint refs present on the configured
45	// checkpoint remote (names only, via `ls-remote refs/entire/checkpoints/*` — no
46	// object transfer), returning their full ref names. The git-refs store uses it
47	// in List to discover checkpoints written on another machine that have no local
48	// ref yet; each discovered checkpoint is then hydrated lazily on read via
49	// RefFetchFunc. The checkpoint package cannot resolve the remote target itself,
50	// so the CLI layer injects it.
51	//
52	// Scope is stricter than the on-demand read fetch: with no checkpoint_remote
53	// configured the lister returns (nil, nil) and List stays local-only. The
54	// on-demand fetch (FetchURL) falls back to origin in that case. When a
55	// checkpoint_remote is configured the lister queries the resolved checkpoint
56	// URL (which can still fall through to origin in FetchURL edge cases).
57	type RemoteRefListFunc func(ctx context.Context) ([]plumbing.ReferenceName, error)
58	
59	// FetchingTree wraps a git tree to automatically fetch missing blobs on demand.
60	// After a treeless fetch (--filter=blob:none), tree objects are available locally
61	// but blob objects are not. Each File() call checks whether the target blob
62	// exists locally and fetches it from the remote if missing, using FindEntry
63	// to locate the blob hash without resolving the blob itself.
64	//
65	// Because go-git's ObjectStorage caches the packfile index and never refreshes
66	// it, blobs fetched by external git commands (e.g. git fetch-pack) may not be
67	// visible to go-git's storer. As a fallback, File() reads the blob via
68	// "git cat-file" which always sees the current on-disk object store.
69	//
70	// For best performance, call PreFetch before reading files. PreFetch walks
71	// the tree, identifies locally-missing blobs, and batch-fetches them in a
72	// single network round-trip instead of one fetch per File() miss.
73	type FetchingTree struct {
74		inner  *object.Tree
75		ctx    context.Context
76		storer storer.EncodedObjectStorer
77		fetch  BlobFetchFunc
78	}
79	
80	// NewFetchingTree wraps a git tree with on-demand blob fetching.
81	// The storer is used to check if blobs exist locally, and fetch is called
82	// to download any that are missing. If fetch is nil, File() behaves
83	// identically to the underlying tree.
84	func NewFetchingTree(ctx context.Context, tree *object.Tree, s storer.EncodedObjectStorer, fetch BlobFetchFunc) *FetchingTree {
85		return &FetchingTree{
86			inner:  tree,
87			ctx:    ctx,
88			storer: s,
89			fetch:  fetch,
90		}
91	}
92	
93	// File returns the file at the given path. Resolution order:
94	//  1. go-git's storer (fast path, in-memory).
95	//  2. `git cat-file -p` against the on-disk object store (handles
96	//     partial-clone-filtered blobs that go-git can't see, plus packfiles
97	//     created by external git commands after this process opened the repo).
98	//  3. Remote fetch via the configured fetcher, then cat-file again.
99	//
100	// Trying cat-file BEFORE the remote fetch is critical: in partial-clone
101	// repos, blobs are commonly on disk but invisible to go-git's storer
102	// (filtered out, or in a packfile not in go-git's index cache). Without
103	// this short-circuit, every File() would burn a multi-second network
104	// round-trip even though the blob is already local.
105	func (t *FetchingTree) File(path string) (*object.File, error) {
106		if file, err := t.inner.File(path); err == nil {
107			return file, nil
108		}
109	
110		entry, findErr := t.inner.FindEntry(path)
111		if findErr != nil {
112			logging.Debug(t.ctx, "FetchingTree.File: entry not found",
113				slog.String("path", path),
114				slog.String("error", findErr.Error()),
115			)
116			return nil, findErr //nolint:wrapcheck // return original error
117		}
118	
119		if file, gitErr := t.readFileViaGit(path, entry); gitErr == nil {
120			return file, nil
121		}
122	
123		if t.fetch == nil {
124			return nil, fmt.Errorf("blob %s not available locally and no fetcher configured", entry.Hash.String()[:12])
125		}
126	
127		logging.Debug(t.ctx, "FetchingTree.File: blob missing locally, fetching from remote",
128			slog.String("path", path),
129			slog.String("hash", entry.Hash.String()[:12]),
130		)
131		if fetchErr := t.fetch(t.ctx, []plumbing.Hash{entry.Hash}); fetchErr != nil {
132			logging.Warn(t.ctx, "FetchingTree.File: blob fetch failed",
133				slog.String("path", path),
134				slog.String("hash", entry.Hash.String()[:12]),
135				slog.String("error", fetchErr.Error()),
136			)
137			return nil, fetchErr
138		}
139	
140		if file, err := t.inner.File(path); err == nil {
141			return file, nil
142		}
143	
144		logging.Debug(t.ctx, "FetchingTree.File: storer cache stale, reading via git cat-file",
145			slog.String("path", path),
146			slog.String("hash", entry.Hash.String()[:12]),
147		)
148		return t.readFileViaGit(path, entry)
149	}
150	
151	// PreFetch walks the tree recursively, identifies blob entries that are missing
152	// from the local object store, and batch-fetches them in a single call to
153	// t.fetch. This avoids per-blob network round-trips during subsequent File()
154	// calls. It is safe to call even when all blobs are already local (no-op).
155	// Returns the number of blobs fetched.
156	func (t *FetchingTree) PreFetch() (int, error) {
157		if t.fetch == nil || t.storer == nil {
158			return 0, nil
159		}
160	
161		missing := t.collectMissingBlobs(t.inner)
162		if len(missing) == 0 {
163			return 0, nil
164		}
165	
166		logging.Debug(t.ctx, "FetchingTree.PreFetch: batch-fetching missing blobs",
167			slog.Int("count", len(missing)),
168		)
169	
170		if err := t.fetch(t.ctx, missing); err != nil {
171			return 0, fmt.Errorf("prefetch %d blobs: %w", len(missing), err)
172		}
173	
174		return len(missing), nil
175	}
176	
177	// CollectMissingBlobs returns the hashes of every blob entry in this tree
178	// (recursively) that isn't present in the local object store. Useful for
179	// callers that want to decide whether network work is needed before
180	// running PreFetch (e.g., to avoid showing a spinner in fast no-op cases).
181	func (t *FetchingTree) CollectMissingBlobs() []plumbing.Hash {
182		return t.collectMissingBlobs(t.inner)
183	}
184	
185	// collectMissingBlobs recursively walks a tree and returns hashes of blob
186	// entries that are not present in the local object store.
187	func (t *FetchingTree) collectMissingBlobs(tree *object.Tree) []plumbing.Hash {
188		var missing []plumbing.Hash
189		for _, entry := range tree.Entries {
190			if entry.Mode.IsFile() {
191				if t.storer.HasEncodedObject(entry.Hash) != nil && !t.blobOnDisk(entry.Hash) {
192					missing = append(missing, entry.Hash)
193				}
194			} else {
195				// Recurse into subtrees (tree objects are local after treeless fetch).
196				subtree, err := tree.Tree(entry.Name)
197				if err == nil {
198					missing = append(missing, t.collectMissingBlobs(subtree)...)
199				}
200			}
201		}
202		return missing
203	}
204	
205	// blobOnDisk returns true if `git cat-file -e <hash>` finds the blob in
206	// the local object store. Used as a second-opinion check before deciding
207	// a blob needs to be fetched: in partial-clone repos a blob can be on
208	// disk but invisible to go-git's storer (filtered out, or in a packfile
209	// not in the cached index). We'd rather skip a wasted network round-trip.
210	func (t *FetchingTree) blobOnDisk(hash plumbing.Hash) bool {
211		cmd := exec.CommandContext(t.ctx, "git", "cat-file", "-e", hash.String())
212		return cmd.Run() == nil
213	}
214	
215	// readFileViaGit reads a blob via "git cat-file -p <hash>" and returns an
216	// in-memory *object.File. This bypasses go-git's storer which may have a
217	// stale packfile index after external git commands fetched new objects.
218	func (t *FetchingTree) readFileViaGit(path string, entry *object.TreeEntry) (*object.File, error) {
219		cmd := exec.CommandContext(t.ctx, "git", "cat-file", "-p", entry.Hash.String())
220		content, cmdErr := cmd.Output()
221		if cmdErr != nil {
222			logging.Warn(t.ctx, "FetchingTree.readFileViaGit: cat-file failed",
223				slog.String("path", path),
224				slog.String("hash", entry.Hash.String()[:12]),
225				slog.String("error", cmdErr.Error()),
226			)
227			return nil, fmt.Errorf("blob %s not readable after fetch: %w", entry.Hash.String()[:12], cmdErr)
228		}
229	
230		// Create an in-memory encoded object to construct the File.
231		memObj := &plumbing.MemoryObject{}
232		memObj.SetType(plumbing.BlobObject)
233		memObj.SetSize(int64(len(content)))
234		w, wErr := memObj.Writer()
235		if wErr != nil {
236			return nil, fmt.Errorf("memory object writer: %w", wErr)
237		}
238		if _, wErr = w.Write(content); wErr != nil {
239			return nil, fmt.Errorf("memory object write: %w", wErr)
240		}
241		if wErr = w.Close(); wErr != nil {
242			return nil, fmt.Errorf("memory object close: %w", wErr)
243		}
244	
245		blob := &object.Blob{}

# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
- Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
- Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
- Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
- Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
| "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Final Rule

```
Production code → test exists and failed first
Otherwise → not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

18	// remote.<name>.promisor=true and remote.<name>.partialclonefilter=blob:none
19	// into .git/config. That is sticky across future fetches on the same remote
20	// (including the user's regular `git fetch origin` / `git pull`), turning
21	// origin into a promisor remote and changing fetch behavior repo-wide.

28	
29		cmd := &cobra.Command{

31			Short: "Diagnose and fix session issues",
32			Long: `Scan for session issues and offer to fix them.
33	
34	Checks performed:
35	  1. Disconnected metadata branches: detects when local and remote
36	     entire/checkpoints/v1 branches share no common ancestor (caused by a
37	     previous bug). Fixes by cherry-picking local checkpoints onto remote tip.
38	
39	  2. Operational logs: warn when .entire/logs cannot be written. Every other
40	     diagnostic is delivered by writing there, and that write is silent about
41	     its own failure, so an unwritable log directory looks exactly like a repo
42	     where nothing ran.
43	
44	  When Codex hooks are installed:
45	  3. Codex hook trust: warn when hooks declared in .codex/hooks.json
46	     lack a trusted_hash entry in the user's Codex config (i.e. /hooks
47	     review hasn't run yet on this machine, or a newer entire release
48	     added a hook the user hasn't approved yet).
49	
50	  For each installed agent that reports hook-config drift:
51	  4. Hook config: warn when the installed hooks no longer match what this
52	     CLI writes (e.g. an older release wrote Claude Code tool matchers that
53	     no longer fire, or a committed Pi/OpenCode extension has gone stale).
54	     Fix by re-running 'entire enable --force'.
55	
56	  5. Stuck sessions: sessions stuck in ACTIVE or ENDED phase that need cleanup.
57	
58	A session is considered stuck if:
59	  - It is in ACTIVE phase with no interaction for over 1 hour
60	  - It is in ENDED phase with uncondensed checkpoint data on a shadow branch
61

63	  - Condense: Save session data to permanent storage
64	  - Discard: Remove the session state and shadow branch data
65	  - Skip: Leave the session as-is

68	be condensed will be discarded.

576	//
577	// This is the one hook surface a user cannot see going wrong. Agent hook configs
578	// are committed files that turn up in a diff; .git/hooks is per-clone and
579	// untracked, so pulling a release that changes hook generation never touches it.
580	// A hook left by the removed local-dev mode still carries Entire's marker, so it

587	// reinstall is content-idempotent, backs up any foreign hook it displaces, and
588	// writes exactly what the next turn-start would write anyway. Someone reaching
589	// for doctor after a rejected push wants to be unblocked, not handed a second
590	// command to run.
591	func checkGitHooks(cmd *cobra.Command, force bool) error {
592		ctx := cmd.Context()
593		w := cmd.OutOrStdout()
594	
595		switch strategy.CheckGitHookState(ctx) {
596		case strategy.GitHooksCurrent:
597			fmt.Fprintln(w, "✓ Git hooks: OK")
598			return nil
599	
600		case strategy.GitHooksAbsent:
601			// Missing hooks are only a problem where Entire was actually set up.
602			// doctor runs in any git repo, so treating this as actionable would let
603			// `entire doctor --force` install hooks into — and back up the existing
604			// hooks of — a repo that never opted in. That is the loudest possible
605			// surprise from a diagnostic command. The sibling checks already hold this
606			// line: checkHookDrift stays silent on HooksAbsent, and
607			// checkCodexHookTrust returns early when there is no codex hooks file.
608			//
609			// IsSetUpAny rather than IsSetUpAndEnabled: a repo that ran `entire
610			// disable` still wants working hooks, because the hooks themselves are
611			// what no-op while disabled.
612			if !settings.IsSetUpAny(ctx) {
613				return nil
614			}
615			fmt.Fprintln(w, "Git hooks: NOT INSTALLED")
616			fmt.Fprintln(w, "  Commits in this repository are not captured as checkpoints.")
617	
618		case strategy.GitHooksOutdated:
619			// Actionable whatever the settings say: a hook carrying Entire's marker
620			// means this repo opted in at some point, and a stale one is actively
621			// broken rather than merely missing.
622			fmt.Fprintln(w, "Git hooks: OUT OF DATE")
623			fmt.Fprintln(w, "  A hook still runs Entire from the working tree instead of the installed")
624			fmt.Fprintln(w, "  binary. This can reject `git push`, because the path it names is gone.")
625		}
626		fmt.Fprintln(w, "  Fix: reinstall the managed git hooks (any non-Entire hook is backed up).")
627	
628		if !force {
629			// Degrade to warn-only when there is nobody to ask. An agent or CI run
630			// must not be blocked on a prompt, and rewriting a repo's hooks
631			// unasked is worse than naming the command that does it.
632			if !interactive.CanPromptInteractively() {
633				fmt.Fprintln(w, "  Run `entire doctor --force` to apply it.")
634				return nil
635			}
636			proceed, promptErr := confirmDoctorFix(ctx, w, "Reinstall Entire git hooks?")
637			if promptErr != nil {
638				return promptErr
639			}
640			if !proceed {
641				return nil
642			}
643		}
644	
645		if _, err := strategy.ReinstallGitHooks(ctx); err != nil {
646			return fmt.Errorf("failed to reinstall git hooks: %w", err)
647		}
648		fmt.Fprintln(w, "  ✓ Fixed: git hooks reinstalled")
649		return nil
650	}

652	// checkLogSink reports a .entire/logs Entire cannot write to.
653	//
654	// Every other diagnostic in the CLI is delivered by writing there, and that
655	// write is deliberately silent about its own failure — a dropped log line must
656	// never surface as an error in the caller. So an unwritable log directory
657	// presents exactly like a repo where nothing ever ran: no message, exit 0, and
658	// an absent or empty entire.log. That is the shape of the support report this
659	// logging work exists to fix, so doctor is the wrong command to reproduce it.
660	//
661	// Read-only. The fixes are ownership and permissions, which doctor cannot take
662	// on the user's behalf.
663	//
664	// A nil logger means the entry point declined to build one, i.e. Entire was
665	// never set up here — nothing to nag about, and reading it back from the
666	// context is what keeps this check on the same directory the logger actually
667	// uses instead of re-deriving the path.
668	func checkLogSink(cmd *cobra.Command) {
669		err := logging.LoggerFromContext(cmd.Context()).EnsureOpen()
670		if err == nil {
671			return
672		}
673	
674		w := cmd.OutOrStdout()
675		fmt.Fprintln(w, "Operational logs: NOT WRITABLE")
676		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  %v\n", err)
677		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Entire's diagnostics are being dropped, including the redaction warnings\n")
678		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  that explain why a custom rule isn't matching. `entire doctor logs` and\n")
679		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  `entire doctor bundle` have nothing to report until this is fixed.\n")
680		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  Fix: resolve the error above so %s is a writable directory — commonly\n", logging.LogsDir)
681		fmt.Fprintln(w, "  ownership or permissions, a regular file occupying the path, or a full disk.")

230	// gitHookStateInHooksDir classifies the hooks in the given directory. A hook that
231	// is present but still invokes a removed local-dev launcher reads Outdated, not
232	// Current, which is what makes EnsureSetup reinstall it rather than leaving a
233	// broken hook in place forever.
234	func gitHookStateInHooksDir(hooksDir string) GitHookState {
235		outdated := false
236		for _, hook := range gitHookNames {
237			hookPath := filepath.Join(hooksDir, hook)
238			data, err := os.ReadFile(hookPath) //nolint:gosec // Path is constructed from constants
239			if err != nil {
240				return GitHooksAbsent
241			}
242			content := string(data)
243			if !strings.Contains(content, entireHookMarker) {
244				return GitHooksAbsent
245			}
246			if entireHookLineRunsFromWorkingTree(content) {
247				outdated = true
248			}
249		}
250		if outdated {
251			return GitHooksOutdated
252		}
253		return GitHooksCurrent
254	}

256	// entireHookLineRunsFromWorkingTree reports whether the hook's OWN Entire
257	// invocation names a legacy launcher.
258	//
259	// Scoped to the invocation line, not the whole file. A user may hand-edit a hook
260	// Entire installed to append their own steps, and one of those steps containing
261	// `go run ` must not make the file read as ours-but-stale: InstallGitHook only
262	// backs up a hook that does NOT carry entireHookMarker, so a hand-edited hook is
263	// rewritten with no backup and a false positive here would silently discard their
264	// additions. Every generated invocation contains `hooks git `, so keying on that
265	// line separates Entire's command from anything around it.
266	func entireHookLineRunsFromWorkingTree(content string) bool {

The parent clarifies the ~1,800 requests came from git's own lazy-fetch loop, one fetch per probe, rather than a helper-internal retry. So ENCLI-335's core issue is that when the server returns 503 with Retry-After for a want, the client can never succeed and never stops — I'm trying to pin down whether that "never stops" comes from git itself retrying on 503, since in the AU incident each probing git command spawned fetch after fetch, but I'm unsure if git actually honors Retry-After and loops on a single want.

Actually the real retry surface is doWithFailover: on a 503, shouldFailover marks the node failed and tries the next node, meaning a single bogus want gets sent to all five serving nodes — which matches the "all five serving nodes equally" detail — and markNodeFailed churns the healthy replica cache by marking everything failed. So the fix should center on bounding that retry/failover behavior, though I still need to check whether there's a separate unbounded retry loop elsewhere, like in push.go's queued refs handling, since the ticket specifically claims no backoff and no ceiling.

No client-side code respects Retry-After, and each subsequent git command just re-triggers the fetch with no memory of prior failures. Actually the per-request node fan-out is bounded by node count, so it's not truly infinite — meaning the real unbounded retry culprit might be elsewhere, like in FetchBlobsByHash or a similar call path I should check next.

This really is one of those cases where I should list plausible explanations and ask the user rather than guess further. Before doing that though, let me do one more targeted search for retry loops across push.go, list.go, connect.go, the CLI's pre-push logic, and main.go of git-remote-entire.

input.prompt:
In the repo /Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/cli/stuttgart (Go, the Entire CLI), I'm investigating ticket ENCLI-335 which claims: "git-remote-entire retries a failed want with no backoff and no ceiling, and the entireio/cli pre-push hook's `|| true` hides the failure entirely. When the server answers 503 + Retry-After: 5 for a want it has never held, the client can never succeed and never stops."

Search breadth: very thorough. Find every code path that could produce repeated/unbounded retries of a failed git-upload-pack or git-receive-pack request, and every place a checkpoint push/fetch failure is swallowed. Specifically:

1. In cmd/git-remote-entire/ and internal/remotehelper/ (githelper, transport, gitproto packages): any loop that re-attempts an HTTP request or a git protocol command after failure — beyond the single-pass node failover in transport/proxy.go doWithFailover. Look at githelper/push.go, run.go, connect.go, list.go, refadv_cache.go, transport.go. Does anything honor Retry-After or sleep-and-retry? Does anything loop until success?

2. In cmd/entire/cli (especially strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go pre-push handling, checkpoint push queue in checkpoint/ or strategy/, plugin_gitremote.go, explain.go FetchBlobsByHash): where are checkpoint push/fetch failures logged-and-swallowed instead of surfaced? Is there a queued-refs mechanism that retries the same failed ref push on every subsequent push forever? Where exactly is the swallow (file:line)?

3. Any shell command construction containing `|| true` related to push, or Go code that deliberately ignores push errors on the pre-push path.

Report: (a) each retry loop found with file:line and its bound (or lack of one), (b) each swallow point on the pre-push/checkpoint-push path with file:line and what message the user sees (if any), (c) whether anything client-side reads the Retry-After header. Max 8 findings, be precise with file:line.

content.text:
## Verdict on ENCLI-335

Two of the ticket's three claims are **factually wrong** against this tree; the third is real but mislocated.

- **`|| true` on pre-push: does not exist.** `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/hooks.go:304` emits `pre-push "$1"` bare. The other four hooks get `|| true` (`hooks.go:282-285`); pre-push is deliberately excluded, with a 14-line comment at `hooks.go:286-299` explaining why (OPF privacy failures must abort `git push`). `hooks_git_cmd.go:338-341` propagates `hookErr` verbatim. The only `|| true` on a pre-push line in the repo is in test fixtures (`hooks_test.go:788`, `881`, `1791`) modelling the removed local-dev launcher.
- **Retry-After: read nowhere.** `grep -rni "retry-after"` over the whole repo (excluding `.git`) returns **zero** hits. No client-side header parse exists to fix.
- **Unbounded retry of a failed want: not in `git-remote-entire`.** Every retry there is single-pass and bounded. The unbounded part is real but lives in the CLI's checkpoint push queue, and it retries *pushes*, not *wants*.

---

### (a) Retry loops found, with bounds

| # | Location | Bound |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `internal/remotehelper/transport/proxy.go:388` `doWithFailover` | `for i := range nodes` — exactly one pass. Failed node removed via `markNodeFailed` (`:265`), so it cannot be re-tried in-process. Terminates at `:467`. |
| 2 | `internal/remotehelper/transport/proxy.go:348` `retryOn401` | Exactly one resend, guarded by `authRetried` at `:386` and by the flat `if != 401 return` at `:349`. Doc at `:344-347` is explicit: "Exactly one retry… there is no loop." |
| 3 | `internal/remotehelper/transport/inforefs.go:51-76` warm→cold fallback | At most two passes (warm failover, then `coldInfoRefs`); `coldInfoRefs` (`:89`) adds at most one Location salvage. |
| 4 | `internal/remotehelper/githelper/connect.go:110`, `stateless.go:60`, `gitproto.go:93/164/245` | All driven by git's stdin; every error path `return`s. Not retry loops — one POST per negotiation round. |
| 5 | **`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_push.go:532`** | Per-ref retry after a failed batch. Bounded per invocation, but `pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery` (`push_common.go:82-95`) is push → fetch+replay → push, so a failing batch costs `1 + 3N` network ops. |
| 6 | **`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/pushqueue.go:37-53`** — **the real "never stops"** | **No bound at all.** No attempt counter, no age eviction, no dead-letter. `Remove` (`:131`) is called only with refs that *landed* (`manual_commit_push.go:544,547`). The only pruning is `partitionLocalRefs` (`push_common.go:29-45`), which drops a ref **only** on `plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound`; the `default:` branch at `:38-42` deliberately *keeps* the ref on any other error. So a ref that exists locally but is permanently unpushable is re-attempted on **every subsequent `git push`, forever**. |

**Aggravating case:** `doPushRef` special-cases `protectedRefError` and gives up (`push_common.go:187-191`), but `flushCheckpointRefsQueue` has **no equivalent** — only `nonInteractiveSSHAuthFailure` short-circuits (`manual_commit_push.go:510-517`). A GH013-protected `refs/entire/*` ref therefore stays queued permanently and pays batch + fetch + per-ref push on every push.

None of these sleep. There is no backoff anywhere on the push path (`grep time.Sleep` over `internal/remotehelper` + `cmd/entire/cli/strategy` → only `cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go:486`, a shutdown-hint timer, and `checkpoint/shadow_ref.go`, a CAS jitter unrelated to network).

### (b) Swallow points on the pre-push / checkpoint-push path

1. **`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_push.go:412-414`** — the primary swallow. `logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs pre-push: checkpoint ref push failed; refs left queued", …)` then `return nil`. `logging.Warn` (`logging/logger.go:221`) goes to `.entire/logs/`, **not** the terminal. The user's only terminal signal is the earlier progress line `[entire] Checkpoint ref push failed; retrying N ref(s) individually...` (`:528`) followed by `" pushed 0 of N"` (`:546`) — no error text, no cause, no remediation.
2. **`manual_commit_push.go:380-383`** — `open repo failed; skipping checkpoint push` → `return nil`. **Completely silent** to the user.
3. **`manual_commit_push.go:390-392`** — policy gate blocks → bare `return nil`. Reaches stderr only if `interactive.CanPromptInteractively()` (`checkpoint_policy.go:59-62`); in a pre-push hook that is typically false, so it degrades to a log line at `checkpoint_policy.go:63-65`.
4. **`manual_commit_push.go:534-535`** — per-ref failure inside the retry loop: log-only warn, `continue`. No stderr unless it happens to be an SSH auth failure (`:536-538`).
5. **`manual_commit_push.go:499-502` / `:547-550`** — `queue.Remove` failure log-swallowed. Consequence: successfully-pushed refs stay queued and are re-pushed forever too.
6. **`push_common.go:161-167` + `:168-240`** — `doPushRef`'s error is documented as *always nil on failure* ("fail-soft by design"). This is the v1/git-branch path; it at least prints `[entire] Warning: …` to stderr at `:197`, `:215`, `:231`. The git-refs path is the quieter of the two.
7. **`git_operations.go:781-792`** (`FetchBlobsByHash`) — per-target failures are `logging.Debug` only; bounded by `chainBudget` (`:754`) and `ReadChainLoopBudget` (`:760`), and the final error *is* returned at `:797`. Not an unbounded or silent path.
8. **Not a swallow:** `hooks_git_cmd.go:324-341` correctly returns `fmt.Errorf("pre-push: %w", hookErr)`.

### (c) Retry-After

Nothing client-side reads it. `transport/proxy.go:260` `shouldFailover` keys purely on `statusCode >= 500`, so a `503 + Retry-After: 5` is treated as a **node health failure**: the node is evicted (`:450`), `OnNodeFailed` fires (persisting the shrunken set via `replicas/replicas.go:93`), and the identical body is re-POSTed to the next replica **immediately, with zero delay**. For a want the cluster has never held, that burns every replica in one pass and then returns `all N nodes failed` (`:467`) — wrong classification and no honoring of the server's pacing hint, but it does terminate.

### Suggested reframing of the ticket

The user-visible symptom is real, but the mechanism is: a permanently-failing checkpoint ref is retried once per `git push` forever because `PushQueue` has no attempt ceiling, and the failure is reported only to `.entire/logs/` (`manual_commit_push.go:412`), so the user sees `pushed 0 of N` and nothing else. Fix candidates: add an attempt/age cap or dead-letter to `pushqueue.go`, extend the `protectedRefError` give-up from `push_common.go:187` into `flushCheckpointRefsQueue`, escalate `manual_commit_push.go:412` to stderr, and teach `shouldFailover`/`doWithFailover` to distinguish `503 + Retry-After` from a dead node.

| 4 | `internal/remotehelper/githelper/connect.go:110`, `stateless.go:60`, `gitproto.go:93/164/245` | All driven by git's stdin; every error path `return`s. Not retry loops — one POST per negotiation round. |
| 5 | **`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_push.go:532`** | Per-ref retry after a failed batch. Bounded per invocation, but `pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery` (`push_common.go:82-95`) is push → fetch+replay → push, so a failing batch costs `1 + 3N` network ops. |
| 6 | **`cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/pushqueue.go:37-53`** — **the real "never stops"** | **No bound at all.** No attempt counter, no age eviction, no dead-letter. `Remove` (`:131`) is called only with refs that *landed* (`manual_commit_push.go:544,547`). The only pruning is `partitionLocalRefs` (`push_common.go:29-45`), which drops a ref **only** on `plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound`; the `default:` branch at `:38-42` deliberately *keeps* the ref on any other error. So a ref that exists locally but is permanently unpushable is re-attempted on **every subsequent `git push`, forever**. |

**Aggravating case:** `doPushRef` special-cases `protectedRefError` and gives up (`push_common.go:187-191`), but `flushCheckpointRefsQueue` has **no equivalent** — only `nonInteractiveSSHAuthFailure` short-circuits (`manual_commit_push.go:510-517`). A GH013-protected `refs/entire/*` ref therefore stays queued permanently and pays batch + fetch + per-ref push on every push.

None of these sleep. There is no backoff anywhere on the push path (`grep time.Sleep` over `internal/remotehelper` + `cmd/entire/cli/strategy` → only `cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go:486`, a shutdown-hint timer, and `checkpoint/shadow_ref.go`, a CAS jitter unrelated to network).

### (b) Swallow points on the pre-push / checkpoint-push path

1. **`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_push.go:412-414`** — the primary swallow. `logging.Warn(ctx, "git-refs pre-push: checkpoint ref push failed; refs left queued", …)` then `return nil`. `logging.Warn` (`logging/logger.go:221`) goes to `.entire/logs/`, **not** the terminal. The user's only terminal signal is the earlier progress line `[entire] Checkpoint ref push failed; retrying N ref(s) individually...` (`:528`) followed by `" pushed 0 of N"` (`:546`) — no error text, no cause, no remediation.
2. **`manual_commit_push.go:380-383`** — `open repo failed; skipping checkpoint push` → `return nil`. **Completely silent** to the user.
3. **`manual_commit_push.go:390-392`** — policy gate blocks → bare `return nil`. Reaches stderr only if `interactive.CanPromptInteractively()` (`checkpoint_policy.go:59-62`); in a pre-push hook that is typically false, so it degrades to a log line at `checkpoint_policy.go:63-65`.
4. **`manual_commit_push.go:534-535`** — per-ref failure inside the retry loop: log-only warn, `continue`. No stderr unless it happens to be an SSH auth failure (`:536-538`).
5. **`manual_commit_push.go:499-502` / `:547-550`** — `queue.Remove` failure log-swallowed. Consequence: successfully-pushed refs stay queued and are re-pushed forever too.
6. **`push_common.go:161-167` + `:168-240`** — `doPushRef`'s error is documented as *always nil on failure* ("fail-soft by design"). This is the v1/git-branch path; it at least prints `[entire] Warning: …` to stderr at `:197`, `:215`, `:231`. The git-refs path is the quieter of the two.
7. **`git_operations.go:781-792`** (`FetchBlobsByHash`) — per-target failures are `logging.Debug` only; bounded by `chainBudget` (`:754`) and `ReadChainLoopBudget` (`:760`), and the final error *is* returned at `:797`. Not an unbounded or silent path.
8. **Not a swallow:** `hooks_git_cmd.go:324-341` correctly returns `fmt.Errorf("pre-push: %w", hookErr)`.

### (c) Retry-After

Nothing client-side reads it. `transport/proxy.go:260` `shouldFailover` keys purely on `statusCode >= 500`, so a `503 + Retry-After: 5` is treated as a **node health failure**: the node is evicted (`:450`), `OnNodeFailed` fires (persisting the shrunken set via `replicas/replicas.go:93`), and the identical body is re-POSTed to the next replica **immediately, with zero delay**. For a want the cluster has never held, that burns every replica in one pass and then returns `all N nodes failed` (`:467`) — wrong classification and no honoring of the server's pacing hint, but it does terminate.

### Suggested reframing of the ticket

The user-visible symptom is real, but the mechanism is: a permanently-failing checkpoint ref is retried once per `git push` forever because `PushQueue` has no attempt ceiling, and the failure is reported only to `.entire/logs/` (`manual_commit_push.go:412`), so the user sees `pushed 0 of N` and nothing else. Fix candidates: add an attempt/age cap or dead-letter to `pushqueue.go`, extend the `protectedRefError` give-up from `push_common.go:187` into `flushCheckpointRefsQueue`, escalate `manual_commit_push.go:412` to stderr, and teach `shouldFailover`/`doWithFailover` to distinguish `503 + Retry-After` from a dead node.

A filtered fetch against a remote name makes git persist
remote.<name>.promisor and remote.<name>.partialclonefilter. Old Entire
releases leaked this config (#712); current ones fetch by URL to avoid
creating it, but never repaired existing leaks. The leak makes ordinary git
commands lazy-fetch missing objects one at a time from a remote that cannot
serve them, and lets \`git gc\` drop local objects — the AU incident's ~28k
probes and the INC-78 amplification.

The config is byte-identical for a leak and a genuine \`git clone --filter\`
partial clone, so the local object store is the tiebreaker:

- No missing objects (verified by a bounded, GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH rev-list
  walk): removal is offered via prompt or --force.
- Missing objects or inconclusive probe: warn-only with copy-paste repair
  steps (refetch, then unset) — never an automatic fix.

URL-keyed sections are skipped: Entire's own filtered fetches create those
deliberately (stampNewlyCreatedRemote).

content.text:
**ENCLI-333 and ENCLI-334 are implemented, tested, and committed** on `inc-78-cli-followups` (two commits, `09c7c62c2` and `7edff7d4c`, based on current main). **ENCLI-335 needs a scope decision from you** — its premises don't match the code.

**ENCLI-333 (the INC-78 trigger)** — `collectMissingBlobs` now batches all candidate hashes through one `git cat-file --batch-check` with `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, and `readFileViaGit` is local-only too. New tests use a fake promisor-remote helper that records lazy-fetch attempts: they reproduced the storm on the old code and prove it's gone. Two things worth knowing:
- The treeless-clone integration test **only passed via the bug**: its settings fixture used a `checkpoint_remote` shape the schema rejects (`provider`+`url`; schema wants `provider`+`repo`), leaving the clone with no valid fetch target — git's lazy fetch was doing all the work. I fixed the fixture to configure a real `origin`, so it now exercises the designed fetch-by-hash path.
- `plugin_gitremote.go`'s single-blob lazy fetch is deliberate and correct (temp clone, promisor holds the blob) — left alone.

**ENCLI-334** — new doctor check. Leak and genuine partial clone are byte-identical in config, so the object store is the tiebreaker: no missing objects (bounded 10s local-only `rev-list` walk) → prompted/`--force` removal; missing or inconclusive → copy-paste repair steps only, never auto-fix.

**Validation**: unit tests, lint, and all 60 Vogon canary tests pass. One integration failure remains — `TestCodexAppServerHooksList_BareWorktreeUsesLayoutRoot` — but it **fails identically on unmodified code** (a `/var` vs `/private/var` TMPDIR symlink mismatch on macOS, from the recently merged codex worktree-hooks PR). Pre-existing; not touched by this work.

**ENCLI-335 — the ticket is wrong in three places** (verified against this tree):
1. The pre-push hook has **no `|| true`** — it deliberately propagates exit codes (OPF must abort pushes).
2. `git-remote-entire` has **no unbounded retry** — every retry is single-pass and bounded.
3. **Nothing client-side reads `Retry-After` at all.**

The real problems behind the symptom: (a) the checkpoint **push queue** (`checkpoint/pushqueue.go`) has no attempt cap — a permanently unpushable ref is retried on every `git push` forever; (b) the failure is swallowed to `.entire/logs` (`manual_commit_push.go:412`), so users see only "pushed 0 of N" with no cause; (c) a `503` makes the failover loop evict **every** replica for a want no node can serve, ignoring the pacing hint. Options: escalate the swallow to stderr (clearly safe), add attempt-based backoff to the queue (product call: skip-with-backoff vs dead-letter, since dropping refs abandons checkpoint data), and/or teach `shouldFailover` about `Retry-After`. Tell me which slices you want, and whether I should rewrite the ENCLI-335 ticket to match the verified mechanics.

Also: I haven't pushed or opened PRs. Say the word and I'll pull latest main and open one PR per ticket (or one combined).
